- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent high), model often overshoots — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% above peak.
- If sentiment is positive (avg > 0.2) and price is trending up, model underestimates upside — add 2–5% to forecast mean for next 7 days.
- When sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive, model lags — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days, aligning with sentiment reversal.
- If model forecast mean is > 10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction: subtract 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak), model often overpredicts — reduce forecast by 3–5% in the 10–15 day window.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (avg between -0.3 and 0.3), model tends to overfit recent noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
